texts.preamble: K.Hashim vs Food Inspector on 11 March, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Friday, The 11Th Day Of March 2016/21St Phalguna, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 34 of 2014 () ------------------------------ Crl.A. 273/2005 of Addl.District Court (Adhoc)-Iii, Thalassery Cc 152/2000 of C.J.M.,Thalassery Revision Petitioners/Appellant/Accused No. 3: --------------------------------------------------------------------------- K.Hashim S/O.T.K.Ibrahimkunhi, Hashim Trading Company Haji Road, Kannur District. By Advs.Sri.T.M.Abdul Latheef Sri.V.R.Nasar Respondents/Respondent/Complainant And State: ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. Food Inspector Thalassery Circle, Thalassery 670 332. 2. State Of Kerala, Represented By The Public Prosecutor High Court Of Kerala, Ernaklulam, Cochin 682 031. R1& R2 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 11-03-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - K.Hashim vs Food Inspector on 11 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20793706/ 1 Crl.R.P. texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 24.2.2000 at about 2 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 gram of toor dal from the shop of the first accused. The second accused was the licensee of the said shop. The third accused was the dealer and the fourth and the fifth accused were manufacturers. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P17 report stating that the sample contained tartrazine and therefore, the same was adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P22 report of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample contained the food colour tartrazine and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts.P1 to P30 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 to DW3 were examined and Exts.D1 to D10 were marked for the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P22 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P22 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food K.Hashim vs Food Inspector on 11 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20793706/ 2 Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
